$comment: Four ways a live grant stops being mergeable. Each case states the observed facts and what the lander must do; none of them is 'merge anyway'. Written against docs/lander.md §The state machine.

expected.shows: range-diff between the approved range and the candidate range, as evidence in the desk item
expected.why: Content identity is the approval. A different patch-id is new content and needs a new sha approval.

expected.shows: the numstat '-' row or the --summary mode change that disqualified the cheap path
expected.why: git patch-id is blind to binary hunks and mode changes, so equal patch-ids prove nothing here. The fence has a hole shaped like a PNG if this case is missed.

expected.shows: the sha the suite tested and the sha the grant approved
expected.why: A green suite on a different merge commit tested a different pair. Re-test; do not merge on someone else's green.

expected.shows: expected parents {baseSha, headSha} and the parents found, as a set
expected.why: The sha matched and the pair was wrong: the base moved before the test. Without the parent-set check the grant authorises a merge against a base nobody tested.
